report_name: Hundreds of French Supermarket Refrigeration Controllers Exposed Online After Hack

attack_patterns.name: Internet Accessible Device
attack_patterns.description: Refrigeration controllers from Danfoss and Copeland were directly exposed to the public internet, providing the initial attack surface for the cyberattack.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely exploited the remote management protocols of the internet-facing Danfoss and Copeland devices, possibly using default or weak credentials to gain access.

attack_patterns.name: Manipulation of Control
attack_patterns.description: Attackers remotely issued commands to the refrigeration controllers to raise their temperature to 50°C, causing food spoilage and fires.

campaigns.name: French Supermarket Refrigeration Attack
campaigns.description: A coordinated cyberattack in October 2026 where an unknown threat actor remotely accessed and manipulated refrigeration controllers in at least 350 French supermarkets, causing widespread food spoilage and fires.
campaigns.objective: Cause physical disruption and damage to French supermarkets by sabotaging refrigeration systems.

identities.name: French Supermarkets
identities.description: A class representing at least 350 supermarkets in France whose industrial refrigeration control systems were targeted in a cyberattack, leading to food spoilage and equipment damage.

identities.name: Danfoss
identities.description: A vendor of industrial control systems whose AK-SM800 series controllers and StoreView remote monitoring panels were targeted in the attack.

identities.name: Copeland
identities.description: A vendor of industrial control systems whose XWeb Pro platform and Dixell XWeb product line were targeted in the attack.

infrastructure.name: Exposed Refrigeration Controllers
infrastructure.description: Internet-exposed Danfoss AK-SM800 and Copeland XWeb Pro refrigeration controllers that were remotely accessed and manipulated by attackers to alter temperature settings.

indicators.name: Exposed Copeland/Dixell XWeb Interface
indicators.pattern:
title: Exposed Copeland/Dixell XWeb Interface
id: 2b8a1c9e-f0b1-4d5e-8c6a-9f7b3d2e1a0c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects web server responses with the title "XWEB EVO", which is indicative of an exposed Copeland/Dixell XWeb industrial control system interface.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/danfoss-fridge-hack-350-controllers-exposed-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t0819
level: high
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    r-body|contains: '<title>XWEB EVO</title>'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects exposed Copeland/Dixell XWeb industrial control system interfaces based on the HTML title 'XWEB EVO', as mentioned in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Exposed Danfoss Web Interface
indicators.pattern:
title: Exposed Danfoss Web Interface
id: 8e3d4f5a-1b2c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects web traffic associated with Danfoss products, which could indicate an exposed industrial control system interface. This is based on the Shodan query `http.component:"Danfoss"`.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/danfoss-fridge-hack-350-controllers-exposed-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t0819
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    r-body|contains: 'Danfoss'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web traffic potentially related to exposed Danfoss ICS interfaces by searching for the vendor name in the HTTP response body.

indicators.name: Potential Danfoss AK-SM Web Interface Traffic
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Danfoss AK-SM Web Interface Traffic
id: c7d8e9f0-a1b2-4c3d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects outbound network traffic on port 20000, which is a common default port for Danfoss AK-SM web interfaces. This could indicate communication with an exposed industrial control system.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/danfoss-fridge-hack-350-controllers-exposed-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-18
tags:
  - attack.t0819
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 20000
    Initiated: 'true'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network traffic on port 20000, a common default for Danfoss AK-SM web interfaces, which could indicate communication with an exposed device.
